rows.b: A 51-foot machine of switches, relays, and shafts that computed ballistics and physics tables automatically. It could multiply in about six seconds and printed its answers on punch cards or type.
Cards punched with people's data are read electrically by pins dipping through the holes into mercury cups. Dials count each category as cards feed through by hand and later by machine.
A box of hard drives on the home network that keeps every photo and file safe with automatic copies. It replaces renting cloud storage.
A regular computer and a quantum processor work as one team on each problem. The classical side handles data and control; the quantum side attacks the hard core.
A box that pairs a small quantum processor with a regular computer, splitting each job: the classical side prepares and the quantum side solves the hard kernel. They iterate together.
